origins.section: A Value Split Across Lines Has a Seam at Every `+`, and a Missing `\n` or Space There Changes It
A Value Split Across Lines Has a Seam at Every `+`, and a Missing `\n` or Space There Changes It
`\n` Is Always a Line Feed; `%n`, `println` and `lineSeparator()` Follow the Platform
A Text Block Removes the Escaped Quotes and the Seams, Not the Backslashes or the Values

recorded.outcome:q-update-with-comment: Page, seam section: 'The line breaks you see in the editor are outside them, so they are not in the string... in the string there is no end of line, and `--` comments out the `WHERE`. A `DELETE` without a condition is valid SQL, so the database deleted every row.' Page shows DELETE, not UPDATE, but the same reasoning carries over directly.

recorded.outcome:q-review-wants-builder:a: Page says `javac` does the folding at compile time ('javac folds each into one string... single ldc'), not the JIT at run time. That refutes the stated reason, even though 'keep the +' is the right decision.

recorded.outcome:q-review-wants-builder:c: Page: 'The `+` itself costs nothing at run time... `javac` folds each into one string.' No String is created per `+` at run time.
recorded.prompt:q-review-wants-builder:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-review-wants-builder:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-review-wants-builder:d: Page: 'javap shows a single ldc per statement', so the expression compiles to one ldc, not a concatenation run on each call. The page never mentions invokedynamic, so the explanation's claim that invokedynamic is used for non-constant expressions is not supported by the page. The option itself is still refuted.
